title: CodeLens
summary: An AST-driven source code intelligence platform for mapping dependencies, uncovering codebase architecture, and enabling informed refactoring through deterministic analysis and repository-grounded AI assistance.
highlights: Built an AST-based parsing engine to extract source structures, resolve module dependencies, and map relationships across the codebase.
Analyzed a repository graph comprising 1,468 nodes, 2,760 edges, and 138 detected architectural communities.
Combined deterministic repository analysis with code-grounded AI documentation to produce context-aware insights without relying on speculative code interpretation.

story.problem: Understanding a medium-to-large codebase is often a matter of piecing together scattered definitions, dependencies, and module relationships. Without a clear architectural picture, even seemingly small changes can require navigating hundreds of files. Traditional documentation also tends to drift away from implementation because it is maintained separately from the source code. CodeLens addresses this gap by deriving architectural insights directly from the code itself.
constraints: Ensure that dependency analysis remains deterministic, avoiding fabricated imports, inferred relationships, or dependencies unsupported by the source code.
Handle repositories containing thousands of files while resolving barrel exports, circular dependencies, and dynamic module references efficiently.
Keep memory consumption under control while performing graph analysis and modularity-based community detection on large dependency networks.

decisions.title: AST Parsing Instead of Regex-Based Extraction
decisions.why: Regular expressions cannot reliably interpret nested scopes, aliased re-exports, or complex language syntax. AST-based parsing provides structured access to source code and a more dependable foundation for dependency extraction.
decisions.tradeoff: Structured parsing introduces greater initial processing overhead than simple string matching, making caching and incremental analysis important for maintaining performance.

decisions.title: Community Detection for Architectural Clarity
decisions.why: Rendering thousands of interconnected modules as a single flat graph quickly becomes difficult to interpret. Modularity-based community detection groups closely related components into meaningful clusters, making larger architectures easier to explore.
decisions.tradeoff: Graph partitioning introduces additional computational overhead and requires efficient graph representations and traversal strategies.

decisions.title: Repository-Grounded AI Assistance
decisions.why: AI-generated explanations are only useful when they reflect the actual structure of a repository. Feeding the model verified dependency relationships and extracted code context helps keep generated documentation anchored to the implementation.
decisions.tradeoff: Context-window limitations require selective extraction of relevant interfaces, relationships, and source structures instead of passing entire files or methods.

story.hardest: Resolving circular dependencies and deeply nested barrel exports without triggering recursive traversal loops, duplicating graph relationships, or exhausting memory during large-scale community detection.
story.mistakes: The initial implementation attempted to render the entire 1,400-node dependency graph in a single SVG pass, causing severe browser performance degradation, with rendering dropping to approximately 4 FPS. The visualization was reworked around hierarchical viewport culling, level-of-detail aggregation, and Web Workers to separate graph layout computation from the main rendering thread.
story.next: Extend language support to Rust and Go, and introduce Git-aware graph overlays that reveal the architectural impact of individual commits and pull requests.

title: Ludo Neo
summary: Synchronized multiplayer board game featuring real-time matchmaking, bot integration, and sub-millisecond state persistence.
highlights: Engineered bidirectional Socket.IO communication to transmit player turns and propagate state in real time.
Implemented automated matchmaking and algorithmic bot fallbacks for low-latency lobbies.
Integrated Redis and RedisJSON for atomic game-state storage, retrieval, and session recovery.

story.problem: Multiplayer board games require authoritative rule enforcement, sub-second turn propagation, and seamless reconnection handling. When players disconnect on unstable mobile networks, games shouldn't freeze, desynchronize, or leave the table in an orphaned, corrupted state.
constraints: Zero trust in client input: all dice rolls, collision validations, and token movements must be strictly validated on the authoritative server.
Seamless session recovery: reconnecting players must restore the board state down to the remaining turn timer without stalling opponents.
Sub-100ms message roundtrip latency even under concurrent room load.

decisions.title: Authoritative Server State Machine with RedisJSON
decisions.why: Storing state in memory on a single process prevents horizontal scaling. RedisJSON allows atomic state mutations and sub-millisecond read/write operations with persistent durability.
decisions.tradeoff: Requires strict synchronization protocols and JSON serializable state machines.

decisions.title: Algorithmic Bot Fallback on Disconnection
decisions.why: Nothing ruins a four-player game faster than one disconnected user causing the match to freeze indefinitely.
decisions.tradeoff: Designing heuristic decision rules for bots that feel fair and competitive without appearing clairvoyant or punishing.

decisions.title: Socket.IO Ack-based Event Acknowledgement
decisions.why: Packet loss or temporary signal dropouts could skip turn notifications. Explicit acknowledgement cycles ensure state synchronization.
decisions.tradeoff: Introduces state machine queues to buffer out-of-order player actions.

story.hardest: Race conditions between player disconnection timers, automated turn timeouts, and reconnect handshakes arriving at the exact millisecond a bot was being assigned.
story.mistakes: Initially sent full board snapshots over WebSockets on every micro-turn. This was wasteful and spiked mobile bandwidth. Refactored to delta action payloads with periodic checksums for validation.
story.next: Implementing WebRTC data channels for peer-assisted audio chat and distributed lobby matchmaking across regional edge nodes.

title: AlgoVisuals
summary: Interactive visualizer illustrating execution flow, traversal order, and structural transformations across algorithms.
highlights: Visualized sorting, searching, binary tree operations, and graph traversal algorithms.
Decoupled pure algorithm execution steps from UI animation loops for deterministic frame playback.
Engineered modular React components representing complex intermediate data structure states.

story.problem: Algorithms are taught with static pseudocode and chalkboard diagrams, leaving students to mentally animate pointer swaps and call stacks. Most interactive visualizers are tightly coupled to timer timeouts, making pause, rewind, step-by-step scrutiny, or speed alterations jerky and error-prone.
constraints: True step-scrubbing: user must be able to drag a scrubber to frame 42 or jump backwards without recalculating UI glitches.
Pure separation between algorithmic execution logic and React render cycles.
Smooth, predictable visual transitions without relying on heavyweight animation libraries.

decisions.title: Generator / Snapshot History Pattern
decisions.why: Running the algorithm eagerly produces an immutable timeline of state snapshots `[State_0, State_1, ... State_N]`. Scrubbing simply indexes into the array.
decisions.tradeoff: Higher initial memory for algorithms with hundreds of intermediate operations, requiring snapshot compaction for large arrays.

decisions.title: Declarative Color and Height State Mapping
decisions.why: Decoupling visual styling (active comparison, pivot, sorted partition) from layout prevents layout thrashing during sorting animations.
decisions.tradeoff: Requires strict synchronization between array indexes and visual key identifiers.

story.hardest: Representing tree balance operations (like AVL rotations and recursive tree traversals) cleanly in 2D space without node overlaps during intermediate rebalancing states.
story.mistakes: Relying on `setTimeout` loops in initial prototypes. Changing speed mid-flight or pressing pause created race conditions where multiple timers fired simultaneously.
story.next: Adding dynamic programming grid matrices and Dijkstra / A* graph traversal pathfinding overlays.

title: Remidos
summary: Cloud-backed task management platform featuring structured CRUD workflows, REST API integration, and cloud persistence.
highlights: Developed responsive client workflows integrated with Express.js REST endpoints.
Engineered schema models in MongoDB Atlas for persistent cloud data storage.
Configured automated deployment pipelines on Render.

story.problem: Most lightweight task trackers either lack real backend persistence or suffer from slow, un-optimistic UI updates where every checkbox toggle blocks on a network roundtrip.
constraints: Seamless cloud sync across devices using MongoDB Atlas.
Clean REST API contracts with robust error boundary fallbacks.

decisions.title: Optimistic UI Mutations
decisions.why: Checkboxes and status toggles update immediately on the client, syncing with Express in the background and rolling back on network failure.
decisions.tradeoff: Requires rollback state buffering in client-side state stores.

story.hardest: Structuring database indexes and schema validation rules to prevent orphan tasks when parent categorization tags are deleted.
story.mistakes: Over-normalizing initial database collections into separate collections for tiny task metadata, leading to avoidable MongoDB aggregation overhead.
story.next: Adding collaborative multi-tenant boards and offline-first IndexedDB synchronization with conflict resolution.
